title: Design-Bid-Build - Rough River Lake Axtel Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP)
description: Solicitation W912QR27BA003 is issued for the demolition and construction of a Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) at Rough River Lake. We request you submit a price proposal for the demolition and construction of a Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) at Rough River Lake. The project duration is estimated at 400 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP). TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This Solicitation will result in one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 237110 - Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition is unrestricted. A 10% Hubzone Price Evaluation Preference will be applied per Clause 52.219-4. SELECTION PROCESS: Basis for award of this Contract will be made based on Lowest Evaluated Price. SOLICITATION WEBSITES: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at federal Contract Opportunities website, https://sam.gov and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module website, https://piee.eb.mil/. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https://sam.gov. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced websites for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the websites periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. The solicitation documents can be downloaded by following the PIEE Solicitation Module Link for W912QR27BA003 Link in the Links / Attachments Section below. REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Kelly Duggins, Kelly.S.Duggins@usace.army.mil. PARTNERING WITH US: https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/ Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/ and then clicking on: View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

All work is to be performed at the Canandaigua, NY VA Medical Center. General scope of work includes: The general scope of this project is to provide any repairs to cracks or degraded asphalt, seal, and then provide new striping to several parking lots surrounding the Canandaigua VAMC. The Canandaigua VAMC requires a Contractor to perform the construction work necessary to accomplish this goal. The Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, services, tools, equipment, and materials required to perform work. title: Ireland – Construction work – National Centre for Research and Remembrance | Phase 3-B Main Works | Main Contractor and Project Supervisor Construction Stage (PSCS)
description: The Phase 3B Main Works development will consist of: a. The change of use of the former Our Lady of Charity and Refuge Convent and Magdalene Laundry to the National Centre for Research and Remembrance (NCRR) (total circa 7510sqm); the provision of a purpose built archival repository (circa 4,030sqm, 2-4 storeys over basement); the provision of 3 storey entrance wing (circa 210sqm) accessed via new shared pedestrian and vehicular entrances from Seán MacDermott Street Lower and Railway Street; and the conservation, refurbishment, and upgrade of the existing convent, chapel and dormitory block (circa 3,490sqm). The development will also include provision of dedicated garden with hard and soft landscaping as a Garden of Reflection (circa 430sqm) and provision of surface bicycle parking; hard and soft landscaping; integrated ESB substation; and all associated site works. The building will include document repositories at basement level, exhibition spaces, conservation laboratories, consultation rooms and a public reading room, offices and meeting rooms. b. The provision of a new Educational Facility (circa 3,690sqm) 3-5 storey block over basement (with rooftop terrace and rooftop plantroom enclosure setback at 3rd and 5th floors respectively). This building will be located to the South West end of the main site (Site A) facing onto Railway Street and accessed via shared new entrance from Railway Street; and will be provided with surface bicycle parking and 3no. bicycle shelters; hard and soft landscaping; a new external courtyard; and all associated site works. The building will include classrooms, workshops, offices and meeting rooms. c. The conservation and refurbishment of the existing derelict 2 storey Dispensary Building to provide a Community based Family and Parenting Support Facility (circa 480sqm); the addition of a new 2 storey extension (circa 275sqm,, total circa 760sqm) to the North side with glazed entrance link accessed from within the NCRR development site; the provision of surface bicycle parking; external bin enclosure; hard and soft landscaping to a new external play space; and all associated site works. The building will include teaching, workshop and play spaces, offices and meeting rooms. d. The provision of a Community based Family and Parenting Support Facility attached to the existing Scots Church (Site B), and to adjoining site 61 Seán MacDermott Street Lower, Dublin 1; the development will include the removal of the existing 2 storey façade; the conservation of the historic Scots Church façade (a protected structure RPS:7480); the provision of new 2 storey extension (circa 435sqm) with rooftop plantroom enclosure setback; a new external play space; and all associated site works.

title: Sources Sought Title II Inspection Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL BUT INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY! This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Respondents will not be individually notified of the results of any government assessments. The 45th Contracting Squadron (45 CONS), is publicizing this Sources Sought Notice to gather industry information and input with respect to the anticipated Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Title II Inspection Services contract in support of 45 Civil Engineering Squadron (45 CES) for Cape Canaveral Space Force Station FL (CCSFS), and Patrick Space Force Base FL (PSFB). PSFB and CCSFS anticipate a requirement that is being considered as a set aside to small business. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code proposed 541330 � Title II Inspection Services. The size standard for NAICS is $25,500,000.00. The requirement is to purchase Title II services include those items involving inspecting, monitoring, and evaluating construction activities to validate conformance to plans and specifications, including reviewing, attending meetings as required, evaluating, testing and approving product submittals and shop drawing; direct consultation as-built services, value engineering studies, peer review services, preparation of construction contract modification requirements. These services will support a continuous need to maintain, repair, modify, and construct critical launch and mission facilities, launch and mission support facilities, utility facilities and infrastructure, and ground systems to meet new, continuing and changing mission needs. 45 CONS is currently seeking Small Business firms capable of providing all labor, materials, and equipment to supply Title II Inspection Services. These services shall support a continuous need to maintain, repair, modify, and construct critical launch facilities, launch support facilities, utilities, and ground systems to meet both continuing and changing mission needs. All work shall be done in accordance with requirements contained in the contract specifications, attached drawings, and applicable laws/regulations. This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is in support of market research being conducted by 45 CONS to determine potential sources capable of fulfilling all requirements associated with the Title II Inspection Services Statement of Work (SOW). The purpose of this RFI is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Small Business firms that can support this requirement as a prime contractor. The government requests interested parties to submit a brief description of their company's business size (i.e. annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), or, if applicable based on NAICS code, Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) and Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB)f or small business) anticipated teaming arrangements, and a description of similar services offered to the Government and to commercial customers. (Note: Because this is contemplated as small business competition, all small businesses should respond.) Any responses involving teaming agreements should delineate between the work that will be accomplished by the prime and the work accomplished by the teaming partners. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision.� As stipulated in FAR 15.201, responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. The decision to solicit a contract shall be solely within the Government's discretion. All interested firms are invited to submit a capabilities package (not to exceed 5 pages) that explicitly demonstrates company capability to meet our needs. Respondents are further requested to indicate their status as a Foreign-owned/foreign-controlled firm and any contemplated use of foreign national employees on this effort. Include in your capabilities package your Unique Entity ID (UEI), Cage Code, and System for Award Management expiration date. Responses must be submitted electronically to the following e-mail addresses: eugenia.faulkner_russell@spaceforce.mil and patricia.bates@spaceforce.mil. RESPONSES ARE DUE NO LATER THAN 3 December 2026 by 12:00 pm.

title: H361--LEX Triannual Energy Study and ARC Flash Testing
description: This amendment is to publish Questions and Answers as submitted in accordance with instruction on RFQ 36C24927Q0038 and also to extend the offer due date: 12/03/2026 @ 11:00 (CT). No other changes are made at this time. Questions and Answers Q.1. Page 1 of the solicitation lists November 30, 2027, at 11:00 AM CST, which is also the deadline currently displayed on SAM.gov. However, page 20 of the solicitation states November 30, 2026, at 11:00 AM CT. Could you please confirm the correct quote submission deadline? A.1. See Amendment 36C24927Q0038_0001, offer due date corrected. The date and time shown on page 1 are system-generated, the solicitation deadline remains 11:00 a.m. local time for the contracting office in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Currently (in November), CT (Central Time) or CST (Central Standard Time) are both used, but CST is technically accurate right now because Daylight Saving Time ended in early November, putting the region on Central Standard Time. The offer due date and time is 10/30/2026 @11:00 CT. Q.2. VAAR 852.219-75 is incorporated by reference, and the requirement is solicited under NAICS 238210. Please confirm which limitation on subcontracting applies to this award: services at 50 percent, or special trade construction contractors at 75 percent. Please also confirm whether the signed certificate is to be returned with the quote. A.2. Yes, the clause is included and will be included in the order in full text for completion prior to award. Q.3. For the technical subfactors and for past performance, please confirm whether the Government will consider the personnel, certifications, experience, references and prior studies of a proposed first-tier subcontractor together with those of the prime. A.3. Submit the information in detail as �prime� or subcontractor. FAPIIS (Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System) reports will be evaluated. Q.4. Please confirm that attendance at the November 16 and 17 site visits is optional and is not a condition of submitting a quote. A.4. Attendance is optional. Q.5. Line item 1002 covers emergency repair work if circuits cannot be energized after inspection. Please advise the pricing basis the Government wants for this line item, for example a not-to-exceed amount set by the Government, hourly rates with an estimated quantity, or a single lump sum, so that all quotes are priced on the same basis. A.5. CLIN 1002 provides an estimated amount for emergency repair funding. If emergency repairs become necessary, all repair costs and funding must be approved by the Station and the Contracting Officer (CO) before work is performed. Although the total cost of such repairs cannot be determined in advance, including this CLIN and associated funding is necessary because the Statement of Work (SOW) requires the Contractor to perform emergency repairs when needed and supports the award of the contract. Q.6. Please confirm whether the Government will accept a partial invoice after acceptance of field testing at each campus and a final invoice after acceptance of the studies and final report. A.6. Invoicing is in arrears, no partial invoices are to be accepted prior to all work is completed and final acceptance. Q.7. We would like to know if this is a brand new contract OR if there is (was) an incumbent performing these services. If not brand new, could you please provide the current / previous contract number? A.7. This is a new requirement, although this study is completed triennially the contract does not have any options. Q.8. Can our references be for work our owner performed or managed while at a prior employer? A.8. No employee references are requested. The vendors Past performance is requested. Q.9. Is a Kentucky electrical license required, or will licenses from another state work? A.9. Need to have a master electrician on shift while work is being performed. Kentucky license is required. Q.10. SOW Section 7 calls for oil and coolant samples on "three existing generators." The attachments show at least three at Bowling and six at Sousley. Which three are included? A.10. The VA requests oil and coolant samples on all generators. Q.11. SOW Section 6, item k says emergency repairs are paid by change order or separate PO. What should we put in CLIN 1002? Is connector replacement found during the IR scan in the base price? A.11. See A.5 for CLIN 1002. Yes, connector replacement found during the IR scan is part of the base scope. SOW Section 7 (Infra-Red Scanning) says problem connections shall be replaced with new connectors and/or tightened to the manufacturer's specifications. Q.12. Who approves the consultant for the short-circuit, coordination and arc flash studies, and when? A.12. Technical review by the COR/Engineering Service, will approve the consultant as part of the technical acceptability evaluation. Q.13. SOW Section 6, item h asks for every worker's OEM training documents at the time of offer. With the 5-file, 8 MB limit, can we send a summary with the quote and the full documents before work starts? A.13. SOW Section 6, item h requires OEM training documentation to be submitted at the time of offer. Per SOW Section 2, NFPA 70E qualified person certifications shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer before work begins. Q.14. Is the 4-hour test date set? A.14. TBD Q.15. Will the site visit sign-in sheets and minutes be posted? A.15. No notes or sign in sheet will be posted. Q.16. Scope � Panelboards - SOW Section 3 lists "Distribution Panels" among the equipment to be maintained and tested, while the Equipment List paragraph applies the procedures to all equipment in the attached electrical studies, which include several hundred branch panelboards. Is hands-on maintenance and testing (e.g., torque verification, breaker testing) required on every branch panelboard, or is an energized infrared scan and visual inspection sufficient for branch panelboards, with full testing limited to distribution panels? A.16. Full maintenance and testing in accordance with SOW Section 7 and NETA MTS, including breaker testing and connection torque verification, is required for the switchboards and distribution panels listed in SOW Section 3. For branch panelboards the required scope is an energized infrared scan, a visual inspection and exercising of the breakers. Branch-panel connections or breakers with thermal anomalies or visual defects shall be investigated and corrected per SOW Section 7 (Infra-Red Scanning). Routine de-energized torque verification and breaker testing are not required on every branch panelboard. Q.17. Scope � Panelboards - The Infra-Red Scanning section references bus plugs, panelboards, MCCs and transformers in the Main, Tower and Chiller buildings. Does the infrared scan also apply to the panelboards in the Sousley Division buildings? A.17.Yes it does. Q.18 . Scope � Equipment Inventory - The SOW references a Government-furnished inventory of equipment to be maintained, inspected and tested. Is there an inventory beyond the arc flash study data files and 2023 test reports attached to the RFQ? If so, can it be provided? A.18. The SOW lists a Government-furnished inventory as an attachment. Per the SOW Equipment List paragraph, any equipment in the facility that is not shown in the attached studies shall also be tested and maintained. Mark its information and location on a hard copy of the studies and turn it in with the report. Q.19. Scope � Equipment Inventory - The 2023 test reports include medium-voltage equipment not shown in the arc flash study data files (for example, Bowling Tower and Main Hospital transformers T2�T6, MV switches T1�T4 and network protectors, and the Sousley Building 68 medium-voltage switchgear). Please confirm this equipment is included in both the maintenance/testing scope and the arc flash and coordination study. A.19. Yes. title: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Regulated Medical Waste
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity intends to award a sole-source Firm Fixed Price commercial services bridge contract to the incumbent contractor, Advant-Edge Solutions of Middle Atlantic, Inc. under the authority of 10 USC 3204(a)(1) and RFO sections 6.103-1(b), 6.103-1(c)(2)(i) and 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), on the basis that the continued provision of these highly specialized medical waste disposal services is available from only one responsible source for the required bridge period, and that a change in source for a short-term bridge contract would result in substantial duplication of transition costs to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. The proposed bridge contract will provide continued enterprise Regulated Medical Waste (RMW) collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, manifesting, reporting, and related services for all military medical treatment facilities (including the U.S. Military Entrance Processing Command�s (USMEPCOM�s), Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS), and the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES)) in all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico. The anticipated bridge period of performance is February 1, 2027, through July 31, 2027, with one optional period from August 1, 2027 to 31 January 2028. The bridge contract is necessary to maintain uninterrupted RMW services while the Government completes the competitive follow-on procurement, which is currently in active source selection, and transitions services to the follow-on contractor. The current contract expires on January 31, 2027. While the Government is actively completing the competitive follow-on procurement, conducting a separate competitive acquisition for a short-term bridge contract requires approximately 90 to 120 calendar days of combined acquisition and transition lead time. The Government cannot complete a separate competitive bridge acquisition and physical transition prior to January 31, 2027, without creating an unacceptable risk of a lapse in mission-critical RMW services. In addition, the Government would not recover the duplicated transition and onboarding costs of switching contractors twice within a three-to-six-month window. Accordingly, interested sources that believe they can satisfy the entire enterprise requirement for this short-term bridge period must demonstrate their ability to execute an accelerated transition and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, without interruption to RMW services at all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico locations. Capability statements must describe the source�s proposed transition approach; available staffing, collection containers, transportation assets, treatment and disposal capacity; required permits and licenses; site onboarding process; and measures to mitigate service-continuity risks during the compressed transition period. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract (nor will the Government reimburse any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice). However, interested sources that believe they can meet the full requirement and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, may submit a capability statement to Mr. Luke Burke at luke.e.burke.civ@health.mil POC no later than 2:30 p.m. Eastern Time on December 2, 2026. The Government will evaluate timely capability statements solely to determine whether a responsible source can meet the Government�s requirements within the required timeframe.

title: Y1DA--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base 509-22-701 - EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades - Downtown Division - Construction (VA-27-00011175)
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project for the Charlie Norwood VA Medical Center located in Augusta, GA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Charlie Norwood VAMC is seeking a general contractor to furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision and perform all work necessary to complete the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project. Work includes, but is not limited to, Verify existing conditions prior to commencing work. Coordinate all construction activities with the VA, COR, facility operations, affected services, and other contractors. Protect existing VA facilities, equipment, utilities, infrastructure, patients, staff, and visitors. Maintain required hospital operations and access throughout construction. Provide required infection control, interim life safety, utility shutdown, fire protection, environmental, and safety measures. Coordinate work involving existing electrical, mechanical, telecommunications, information technology, fire alarm, security, and other facility systems. Obtain required approvals before performing work that affects existing VA operations or utility systems. Provide temporary services and protection necessary to maintain facility operations. Perform testing, inspection, startup, commissioning, and verification of installed systems as required by the contract documents. Correct deficiencies identified during inspections, testing, commissioning, and final acceptance. Provide complete as-built documentation and operation and maintenance information as required. as required to complete the scope of this project. All work is to be performed in accordance with the drawings and specifications. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request For Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR Part 14, considering Price only. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAAR Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Provide specific examples that relate aspects of previous projects to the proposed project. Describe specific technical skills and key personnel your company possess to perform the requirements described under description of work. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. Section 6: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) - A PLA is defined as a pre-hire Collective Bargaining Agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). The PLA questionnaire must be filled out and returned with the Sources Sought response. The questionnaire can be found at the end of this document. See FAR Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and FAR Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement for further details. title: Sources Sought Advisory and Assistance Services contract.
description: SOURCES SOUGHT: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL BUT INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY! This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Respondents will not be individually notified of the results of any government assessments. The 45th Contracting Squadron (45 CONS), is publicizing this Sources Sought Notice to gather industry information and input with respect to the anticipated Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity, (IDIQ) Advisory and Assistance Services contract. The locations of services to be provided potentially include all SLD 45 assets: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station FL (CCSFS), Patrick Space Force Base FL (PSFB), Jonathan Dickinson Missile Tracking Annex (JDMTA) FL, Malabar Missile Tracking Annex-FL, and Ascension Auxiliary Airfield South Atlantic (AAAF). However, the majority of the work will occur at CCSFS and PSFB. PSFB and CCSFS anticipate a requirement that is being considered as a set aside to small business. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code proposed 541310 � Architectural Services. The size standard for NAICS is $12,500,000.00. The requirement is to purchase services such Management Consulting, Program & Program Support, Technical & Engineering Services and Independent Assessments. 45 CONS is currently seeking Business firms capable of providing all labor, materials, and equipment to supply services such as, such Management Consulting, Program & Program Support, Technical & Engineering Services and Independent Assessments. These services shall support a continuous need to maintain, repair, modify, and construct critical launch facilities, launch support facilities, utilities, and ground systems to meet both continuing and changing mission needs. This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is in support of market research being conducted by 45 CONS to determine potential sources capable of fulfilling all requirements associated with Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity, (IDIQ) Advisory and Assistance Services contract. The purpose of this RFI is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Business firms that can support this requirement as a prime contractor. The government requests interested parties to submit a brief description of their company's business size (i.e. annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), or, if applicable based on NAICS code, Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) and Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB)f or small business) anticipated teaming arrangements, and a description of similar services offered to the Government and to commercial customers. Any responses involving teaming agreements should delineate between the work that will be accomplished by the prime and the work accomplished by the teaming partners. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision.� As stipulated in FAR 15.201, responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. The decision to solicit a contract shall be solely within the Government's discretion. All interested firms are invited to submit a capabilities package (not to exceed 5 pages) that explicitly demonstrates company capability to manufacture the product that will meet our needs, as by specification not brand name. Respondents are further requested to indicate their status as a Foreign-owned/foreign-controlled firm and any contemplated use of foreign national employees on this effort. Include in your capabilities package your Unique Entity ID (UEI), Cage Code, and System for Award Management expiration date. Responses must be submitted electronically to the following e-mail addresses: eugenia.faulkner_russell@spaceforce.mil and patricia.bates@spaceforce.mil. RESPONSES ARE DUE NO LATER THAN 3 December 2026 by 12:00 pm.

title: Remove and Install Dorm Furniture (Commodity)
description: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform all work required for the purchase, delivery, uncrating, and full setup of dormitory furniture at a designated dormitory facility located at Francis E. Warren AFB, Wyoming. In addition to delivering and installing the new furniture, the contractor shall be responsible for the complete removal, palletizing, and banding of existing dormitory furniture sets, which must be safely transported and staged in the dormitory courtyard for Government disposition. All freight and shipping must be provided under FOB Destination terms directly to Francis E. Warren AFB. The specific items, finishes, and quantities anticipated under this requirement are as follows: forty-eight (48) each Twin XL single beds equipped with locking bed springs, ninety-six (96) each two-drawer underbed stackable storage units, forty-eight (48) each two-drawer nightstands, forty-eight (48) each one-drawer study desks, and twelve (12) each common-area coffee tables, all manufactured in a uniform Cherry Oak finish. Accompanying seating requirements include forty-eight (48) each desk chairs featuring Cherry Oak construction with blue upholstered seat cushions, and forty-eight (48) each recliner lounge chairs in blue upholstery. The contractor shall provide freight charges for one (1) each shipment to FOB Destination to F.E. Warren AFB, Wyoming. The contractor shall also provide a setup and installation fee for one (1) complete job. Lastly, the contractor shall provide a removal, palletizing, and banding fee for one (1) complete job.

title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) – Office space
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about May 1, 2030, with a right of early termination anytime on or after May 1, 2038 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior, plus an option to extend the lease for One (1) additional period of Two (2) years; • approximately 4,281 usable square metres (um2) of office space, and one (1) parking space; • the proposed space must be available approximately 65 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial building; industrial type buildings and those with industrial space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. preference may be given to spaces with any or all of the following: a highly visible storefront space, on a main road, with direct pedestrian access from the street; 3. a minimum of 771 um2 of the proposed space must be located on a floor with public access; preference may be given to spaces located on the main floor; 4. the proposed space must be contiguous within each floor; 5. if the proposed space is offered on multiple floors, consecutive floors are preferred; 6. a dedicated telecommunication room measuring no less than 20.3 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 7. cleaning services will be required during business hours; 8. the proposed space must be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. parking for approximately 25 vehicles must be available to the public within a one (1) block radius of the proposed space; 10. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 11. acceptable space for the installation of bicycle rack(s); 12. the physical characteristics of the lands and the building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; 13. the dimensions of the proposed space must be compatible for efficient design and use; • the proposed space must be located in the city of Edmonton and within the following boundaries (the geographical boundaries include sites on either side of the roads): North: Whitemud Drive NW to 91 Street NW / 91 Street NW to Roper Road NW / Roper Road NW to 34 Street NW East: 34th Street NW South: Ellerslie Road SW West: 170th Street SW / Terwillegar Drive NW In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. This map is to be used for presentation purposes only and is not a legal document • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

title: Replace Elevators at FDC Miami
description: THIS IS A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR INVITATION FOR OFFERORS TO SUBMIT BIDS. THIS NOTICE WILL BE POSTED FOR A MINIMUM OF 15 DAYS PRIOR TO POSTING OF THE SOLICITATION. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) anticipates issuance of solicitation 15BBNF26Q31000001 for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project titled Replace Elevators at the Federal Detention Center (FDC) Miami. FDC Miami is a federal correctional facility located at 33 NE 4th St., Miami, FL 33132. The work to be performed in association with this project includes the following scope: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials and equipment for the Replace Elevators project at FDC Miami. The project includes, but is not limited to, providing all necessary equipment, labor, materials and incidentals to replace four traction and six hydraulic elevators. The Statement of Work included with the solicitation will provide complete requirements for the project. Any secure/locked documents uploaded with the solicitation will require an active vendor registration at https://SAM.gov as well as your Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) associated with your SAM registration. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. The estimated magnitude of the project lies between $5,000,000 - $10,000,000. The magnitude provided is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. It merely conveys that the estimate/budget lies somewhere within that range). The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 238290 with a corresponding small business size standard of $22.0 million. The solicitation will be available approximately October 14, 2026. The solicitation will be distributed solely through the website at www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov. This is a total small business set-aside. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration must be less than or equal to the size standard specified above (see provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of your registration and view the table therein listing NAICS codes and your indicated business size relative to the assigned NAICS code above). Each bidder's SAM registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm that your business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All bidders are urged to double check their SAM registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. This synopsis is intended only for those who would be entering into a Prime contract with the FBOP for the entirety of this project. The FBOP does not award subcontracts. Subcontracts (if applicable/necessary) are the responsibility of the Prime contractor. The FBOP has no privity of the contract with subcontractors. If you have questions about SAM.gov, Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your bid/proposal/offer, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

title: Haulage and Hoist Wire
description: W912EE Haulage and Hoist Wire Supply This is a solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Solicitation Number W912EE27QA003 is being issued as a request for quote (RFQ) with the intent to issue one Firm-Fixed Price Contract. This solicitation is being issued under 100% small business set aside. The NAICS code for this procurement is 332618, Other Fabricated Wire Product Manufacturing, with a size standard of 500 employees. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with regulations at RFO Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District, has a requirement to procure wire rope for the haulage and hoist winches in support of the Dredge Jadwin. The contractor shall provide all plant, labor, equipment, materials, and supplies necessary to furnish the required quantities of wire rope and deliver within 200 days to 2449 Haining Road, Vicksburg, MS. Additional information about the specifications for this equipment is listed in the statement of work. All Offerors shall submit a quote with content as specified herein. Quotes submitted without the specified content may be determined unsuccessful and removed from further consideration. Offers are encouraged to review all clauses that are incorporated into this solicitation. ****SPECIAL ATTENTION SHOULD BE FOCUSED ON RFO 52.212-2 EVALUATION � COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS, AS THIS CLAUSE OUTLINES THE EVALUATION FACTORS AND BASIS FOR AWARD FOR THIS REQUIREMENT. **** The government intends to make one award for one firm fixed price contract. Offers for less than the required delivery will not be accepted. The Government intends to award without discussions while reserving the right to hold discussions if determined advantageous to the Government. Offerors are encouraged to provide their best proposed pricing in their initial offer. Notes to Offerors: BIDDING SCHEDULE MUST BE RETURNED WITH YOUR QUOTE. Quotes shall be submitted electronically via email, to: alexandria.e.long@usace.army.mil. For information concerning this solicitation, contact Alexandria Long at the above email address or by phone at 601-631-5642. You are responsible for reading all information contained in this solicitation and all attachments if any posted with it. Offerors should check the SAM.gov web site often for modifications to this solicitation. Offerors are responsible for ensuring their quotes arrive timely. TECHNICAL INQUIRIES AND QUESTIONS Technical inquiries and questions relating to this solicitation are to be submitted via Bidder Inquiry in ProjNet at (https://www.projnet.org). Offerors are encouraged to submit questions early in the advertisement process, in order to ensure adequate time is allotted to form an appropriate response and amend the solicitation, if necessary. Any questions submitted within the 72 hours window of the solicitation closing date are not guaranteed a response will be proivded. To submit and review inquiry items, prospective vendors will need to use the Bidder Inquiry Key presented below and follow the instructions listed below the key for access. The Solicitation Number is: W912EE27QA003 � Haulage and Hoist Wire The Bidder/Offeror Inquiry Key is: Specific Instructions for ProjNet Bid Inquiry Access: From the ProjNet home page linked above, click on Quick Add on the upper right side of the screen. Identify the Agency. This should be marked as USACE. Key. Enter the Bidder Inquiry Key listed above. Email. Enter the email address you would like to use for communication. Click Continue. A page will then open saying that a user account was not found and will ask you to create one using the provided form. Enter your First Name, Last Name, Company, City, State, Phone, Email, Secret Question, Secret Answer, and Time Zone. Make sure to remember your Secret Question and Answer as they will be used from this point on to access the ProjNet system. Click Add User. title: Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for CNC Machine Repair, Parts, Programming, and Training Services Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD)
description: The Blue Grass Army Depot, CCRI-MII-B Depot Support Branch/Munitions and Industrial Base Directorate Army Contracting Command - Rock Island intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) under the modernized authority of the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO), specifically leveraging RFO 12.201-1(e)(3) and Class Deviation RFO-2025-16. The BPA will facilitate the streamlined, repetitive procurement of services to perform diagnostic troubleshooting, emergency and routine repairs, preventative maintenance, software programming, and operator/programmer training and parts if needed for CNC machines with an average age of 15 to 20 years old for covered systems that include: CNC Machinery: 3 Axis CNC Mill, 2 or 3 axis CNC Lathe, 5 Axis CNC Lathe Robotic Motion Systems & Controllers: FANUC Robots (M-20iA, R-2000iB); FANUC Controllers (M-20iA, R-30iA). Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs): Allen-Bradley, Mitsubishi, Siemens (all variants utilizing industrial ladder/logic software). This combined synopsis and solicitation serves as the official public notice of the Government's intent to establish a BPA. The primary objective is to create a flexible �charge account� with a qualified, responsible source to fulfill anticipated repetitive needs efficiently. This requirement utilizes the North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 811310 Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance with a size standard of $12.5 Million. This BPA shall not obligate any funds. A BPA is not a Contract. In accordance with FAR 12.201-1-3(e)(3)(iv)(B), the Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases made via properly executed BPA Call Orders made under the BPA. The BPA Master Limit is $750,000. No single BPA Call Order shall exceed $250,000 in total cost. Please note, there is no guarantee that any or all requirements for the services described herein will be issued using an established BPA. The full details and applicable provisions and clauses are available in the attachments of this notice.

title: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Regulated Medical Waste
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity intends to award a sole-source Firm Fixed Price commercial services bridge contract to the incumbent contractor, Advant-Edge Solutions of Middle Atlantic, Inc. under the authority of 10 USC 3204(a)(1) and RFO sections 6.103-1(b), 6.103-1(c)(2)(i) and 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), on the basis that the continued provision of these highly specialized medical waste disposal services is available from only one responsible source for the required bridge period, and that a change in source for a short-term bridge contract would result in substantial duplication of transition costs to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. The proposed bridge contract will provide continued enterprise Regulated Medical Waste (RMW) collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, manifesting, reporting, and related services for all military medical treatment facilities (including the U.S. Military Entrance Processing Command�s (USMEPCOM�s), Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS), and the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES)) in all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico. The anticipated bridge period of performance is February 1, 2027, through July 31, 2027, with one optional period from August 1, 2027 to 31 January 2028. The bridge contract is necessary to maintain uninterrupted RMW services while the Government completes the competitive follow-on procurement, which is currently in active source selection, and transitions services to the follow-on contractor. The current contract expires on January 31, 2027. While the Government is actively completing the competitive follow-on procurement, conducting a separate competitive acquisition for a short-term bridge contract requires approximately 90 to 120 calendar days of combined acquisition and transition lead time. The Government cannot complete a separate competitive bridge acquisition and physical transition prior to January 31, 2027, without creating an unacceptable risk of a lapse in mission-critical RMW services. In addition, the Government would not recover the duplicated transition and onboarding costs of switching contractors twice within a three-to-six-month window. Accordingly, interested sources that believe they can satisfy the entire enterprise requirement for this short-term bridge period must demonstrate their ability to execute an accelerated transition and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, without interruption to RMW services at all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico locations. Capability statements must describe the source�s proposed transition approach; available staffing, collection containers, transportation assets, treatment and disposal capacity; required permits and licenses; site onboarding process; and measures to mitigate service-continuity risks during the compressed transition period. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract (nor will the Government reimburse any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice). However, interested sources that believe they can meet the full requirement and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, may submit a capability statement to Mr. Luke Burke at luke.e.burke.civ@health.mil POC no later than 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 3, 2026. The Government will evaluate timely capability statements solely to determine whether a responsible source can meet the Government�s requirements within the required timeframe.

title: Y1DZ--673-901 Brooksville CBOC Renovation Minor Design-Build - Brooksville, FL
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting a market research to identify qualified sources capable of performing a Design-Build (DB) project. Services to include Architect and Engineering (DB A/E) design services, site preparation and DB Construction (DB C) services for the renovation of the Brooksville Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) at the Brooksville VA Clinic located at 14540 Cortez Boulevard, Suite 108, Brooksville, Florida 34613-6001. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs has a requirement for a Design-Build renovation of the Brooksville Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) under Project No. 673-901. The project includes completion of the remaining design effort, validation of existing conditions, preparation of final construction documents, and execution of construction activities necessary to renovate and modernize the facility in accordance with current VA standards, life safety requirements, operational needs, and applicable VA criteria. This Design-Build project includes all necessary architectural, engineering, specialty consulting, commissioning, and construction services required to deliver a complete and operational renovation. The scope includes review and incorporation of prior design documents, infrastructure upgrades to HVAC and electrical systems, OI&T/telecommunications improvements, safety and security enhancements, fire protection improvements, building envelope repairs, roof and water intrusion remediation, and all associated architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, low-voltage, civil, and site-related work. The contractor shall perform comprehensive site investigation and field verification of existing conditions and develop detailed phasing, infection control, containment, and construction logistics plans to support continued operation of the clinic during construction. Work shall be coordinated with facility stakeholders to maintain safe access for patients and staff while minimizing disruptions to healthcare services. Construction barriers, access routes, temporary utility requirements, dust control measures, and shutdown coordination shall be incorporated into the project design and execution. The completed project shall provide modernized and reliable facility infrastructure that supports ongoing clinical operations, improves building performance, addresses life safety and code compliance requirements, mitigates water intrusion and building envelope deficiencies, and enhances telecommunications, security, and fire protection systems throughout the facility. All completed work shall be fully commissioned, tested, and integrated with existing VA systems and infrastructure in accordance with applicable VA standards and requirements. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 36-101-2, Use of two-phase design-build selection procedures. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. The Government anticipates advertising this project in the timeframe of late December 2026 to early January 2027. The VAPM Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $20,000.000.00 and $50,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 740 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all design and construction related services. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, DUNS number and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a statement of interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: Provide a maximum of three (3) projects completed within the last ten years (10) years in which the Offeror s design-build team has worked together on previous design-build contracts similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. Projects must demonstrate a respondent s design-build experience as a prime construction contractor directly responsible to the owner and managing multiple subcontractors. NOTE: If a prime contractor does not have Design-Build experience, they are permitted to provide up to three (3) relevant non-Design-Build projects that are completed in clinical, hospital or other medical related use space similar in size, magnitude, complexity, and scope to this project. The designer for the team may also provide up to three (3) relevant projects that fall under the requested criteria for the project. A maximum total of six (6) projects may be submitted between the D-B and design teams. *All submission requirements for these projects remain the same and are listed above. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than twelve (12) single sided pages, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum that addresses the above information. Please also include a cover page, which includes, at a minimum: the company s name, address, Unique Entity Identifier (if available), socio-economic status, point-of-contact name, phone number, and e-mail address. Responses must include the Sources Sought number and project title in the subject line of their e-mail response. title: Z--Elevator Inspection and Certification Services
description: Elevator Inspection and Certification Services This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ), and it does not obligate the Government to award a contract. The Bureau of Reclamation, Interior Region 10, California Great Basin Region, Central California Area Office (CCAO), is seeking potential sources capable of providing independent elevator inspection and certification services for elevators located at Folsom Dam, Folsom Powerplant, and New Melones Powerplant in California. The Government is conducting market research to determine the availability of qualified firms and to assist in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. The requirement is for Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) services to perform periodic elevator inspections, witness required testing, provide inspection reports, identify deficiencies and recommendations, and provide elevator certifications in accordance with applicable ASME requirements, including ASME A17.1, A17.2, A17.3, and QEI-1 standards. The anticipated contract will consist of a base year and four option years. Inspection services are anticipated to include: - One annual Category 1 inspection for each of the three elevators (unless superseded by a Category 5 inspection). - One periodic six-month inspection for each of the three elevators. - Witnessing of Category 1 and Category 5 testing performed by the elevator maintenance contractor. - Preparation and submission of inspection reports and certification documentation. The anticipated NAICS code for this requirement is 541350 � Building Inspection Services (Size Standard: $11.5 Million). Competition, set-aside decisions, and acquisition strategy may be based on the results of this market research. Interested firms should submit a capability statement addressing their ability to meet the requirements described above. Responses should include: 1. Company name, address, and SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI). 2. Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, 8(a)). 3. Relevant experience performing independent elevator inspection and certification services for commercial, industrial, utility, hydroelectric, or government facilities. 4. Confirmation that proposed inspectors possess current Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) certification and identification of the certifying organization. 5. Ability to perform inspections at Government facilities located in Folsom, California and Jamestown, California. 6. Any experience performing inspections in accordance with ASME A17.1, A17.2, A17.3, and QEI-1 standards. Responses are due: Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 10:00am PT Submit responses to: margaret_jones@ios.doi.gov This notice is for market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract.

title: Jacksonville Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for Jacksonville Harbor. Jacksonville Harbor: The Jacksonville Harbor, FL - FY27 O and M Contract (non-fed sponsor Jacksonville Port Authority (JAXPORT)) for maintenance dredging typically requires hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s) depending on work location in the~ 20-mile federal channel. The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -47 ft MLLW (w/additional depths for required advanced maintenance areas and allowable over depths) and to transport the dredged sediment to both a designated Dredged Material Placement Area (DMPA) known as Bartram Island and the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS) located approximately 6 nautical miles offshore. Dredged material shall be placed upland in Bartram Island Cell F and the Jacksonville ODMDS Release Zone C1 depending on the specific reach to be dredged. The transport distance to the designated placement areas varies significantly, ranging from direct, local placement to a few miles for the upland placement area and up to 6 miles for ocean disposal from the tip of the south jetty. The work is divided into a base and five options. The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within ten (10) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use not later than 220 days after the Contractor receives the notice to proceed. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. Base: 120 calendar days. Option A: 15 calendar days. Option B: 20 calendar days. Option C: 30 calendar days. Option D: 25 calendar days. Option E: 10 calendar days. Complete all work within Cut-17 Sta. 0+00 through Cut-41 Sta. 20+00 (BASE work), which are located within an Outstanding Florida Waters (OFW), no later than May 20, 2027.This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 02 November 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. title: Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for CNC Machine Repair, Parts, Programming, and Training Services Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD)
description: The Blue Grass Army Depot, CCRI-MII-B Depot Support Branch/Munitions and Industrial Base Directorate Army Contracting Command - Rock Island intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) under the modernized authority of the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO), specifically leveraging RFO 12.201-1(e)(3) and Class Deviation RFO-2025-16. The BPA will facilitate the streamlined, repetitive procurement of services to perform diagnostic troubleshooting, emergency and routine repairs, preventative maintenance, software programming, and operator/programmer training and parts if needed for CNC machines with an average age of 15 to 20 years old for covered systems that include: CNC Machinery: 3 Axis CNC Mill, 2 or 3 axis CNC Lathe, 5 Axis CNC Lathe Robotic Motion Systems & Controllers: FANUC Robots (M-20iA, R-2000iB); FANUC Controllers (M-20iA, R-30iA). Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs): Allen-Bradley, Mitsubishi, Siemens (all variants utilizing industrial ladder/logic software). This combined synopsis and solicitation serves as the official public notice of the Government's intent to establish a BPA. The primary objective is to create a flexible �charge account� with a qualified, responsible source to fulfill anticipated repetitive needs efficiently. This requirement utilizes the North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 811310 Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance with a size standard of $12.5 Million. This BPA shall not obligate any funds. A BPA is not a Contract. In accordance with FAR 12.201-1-3(e)(3)(iv)(B), the Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases made via properly executed BPA Call Orders made under the BPA. The BPA Master Limit is $750,000. No single BPA Call Order shall exceed $250,000 in total cost. Please note, there is no guarantee that any or all requirements for the services described herein will be issued using an established BPA. The full details and applicable provisions and clauses are available in the attachments of this notice.

title: Construction Services for Confined Aquatic Disposal Cell Construction and Maintenance Dredging of the Providence River Federal Navigation Project, Providence, Rhode Island.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for the upcoming dredging project located in Providence, Rhode Island. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns as described below. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990. The solicitation for this project is anticipated to be issued on or about 15 March 2027. The construction will begin in September 2027 and is expected to take approximately 2 years to complete. The estimated construction cost is between $80,000,000 and $100,000,000. The Providence River Maintenance Dredging project involves two major sequences of dredging and disposal activities. The first work sequence will be the construction of a new Confined Aquatic Disposal (CAD) cell adjacent to the Providence River. The second work sequence under this contract will include maintenance dredging of the Providence River and Harbor Federal Navigation Project (FNP) to its authorized depths and dimensions. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 5,500,000 cubic yards (cy) of material using closed clamshell buckets for both major sequences of work over the course of two years. The new CAD cell will be in the Edgewood Basin area located adjacent to the Providence FNP (hereafter the �Edgewood Shoals North (ESN) CAD cell�). To access the CAD cell area, an access channel will be dug between the Providence FNP and the CAD cell area. The access channel will be approximately 100 ft wide and -25 MLLW deep. The CAD cell will have surface dimensions of approximately 1000 ft. by 1000 ft. and be dug to a depth of -60 MLLW. The material excavated to build the access channel is generally a mix of sandy silt and shell fragments. Within the CAD cell area the material is generally described as soft grey to black organic silt with some layers of firm sandy silt and some shell fragments and coarse-grained material. Material excavated from the access channel and CAD cell area will be placed at four locations: Port Edgewood Basin, the Fox Point Reach CAD cells, Prudence Island Disposal Site, and the Rhode Island Sound Disposal Site. This work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,200,000 cy to construct thew ESN CAD cell and its access channel, which must be completed before maintenance dredging of the FNP can begin. The maintenance dredging proposed work consists of mechanically dredging the Providence River FNP to the full -40 MLLW depth plus 2-feet of allowable overdepth. 2,300,000 cy (1,200,000 cy required depth, with up to 1,100,000 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting generally of poorly graded medium to fine sand with silt. The dredge material from this maintenance portion of work will be placed in the ESN CAD cell. Environmental coordination and permitting is being completed by the U.S. Army of Engineers, New England District. All dredging and disposal activities for this project have prescribed work windows that incorporate environmental and recreational time of year restrictions. Refer to the Draft Specification Section provided with this announcement for specifics on the time of year work restrictions. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window it is expected that the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of 300,000 CY per 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is requesting responses to the questions below from both small and large businesses[MC1] . Draft drawings showing a concept design plan and draft Specification Section of 01 11 00 SUMMARY OF WORK have been provided with this announcement to help provide more context for the contract work and responses to these questions. Considering the different disposal locations, are there suggestions on a bid structure that will provide for the most accurate costs of different disposal locations? Any draft restrictions that may impact dredging and/or disposal operations? Any concerns on the period of performance of September 2027 to September 2029 considering the environmental windows and amount of work? If so, why? Any comments about the bed leveling planned in the Fox Point Reach? Are there concerns about this part of the plan, if so, why? Interested firms should also demonstrate their project experience, by providing two (2) projects within the last ten years, which meet the following requirements: Dredging by mechanical means demonstrating a minimum production rate of 300,000 cubic yards in one consecutive 30-day period. Experience with placement of dredged material at an open water placement site in New England during the fall/winter months of October through March. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm is proposing to use on the project, and two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the proposed equipment at the production rate listed above. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Bid bond will need to be provided with the bid. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by December 03 , 2026. Responses should be addressed to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 696 Virginia Road, Concord, MA 01742-2751, ATTN: Kyle Hall, or electronically to Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. title: PIGA Float Assembly Repair Program
description: Login at https://piee.eb.mil and search for 'FA821426RB002' to obtain more details.* Documents related to this procurment are only available through PIEE. 1. Executive Summary: Background & Objective The U.S. Air Force has a critical requirement to support the Minuteman III (MMIII) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) by maintaining the operational readiness of the Missile Guidance Set (MGS) to meet warfighter requirements. Specifically, this effort supports the repair line for the Pendulous Integrated Gyroscopic Accelerometer (PIGA) Float Assembly. The PIGA Float is a critical and precise sub-assembly that serves as the heart of the PIGA instrument, enabling it to measure missile acceleration. Each MGS contains three separate PIGA instruments (each housing a PIGA Float). Without this critical component, the ICBM would cease to function properly. The PIGA Float repair effort is a continuous operation necessary to avoid mission degradation. Quality control and precision engineering are paramount due to the strategic importance of the MMIII weapon system. The contractor must maintain stringent quality assurance protocols to guarantee that each repaired PIGA Float meets the rigorous military specifications. 2. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide the necessary personnel, facilities, and expertise to support the PIGA Float Assembly repair line. The primary scope includes: Repair Operations - The re-manufacture, rebuild, and repair of PIGA Float Assemblies. Volume / Throughput - The repair of 96 PIGA Floats per year. Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) - The repair and/or replacement of GFE as required to support continuous operation of the PIGA Float repair line 3. Contract Structure & Period of Performance The Government anticipates awarding an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract utilizing a mix of Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) and Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) pricing arrangements. Contract Duration - 5-Year IDIQ Anticipated Ordering Period - 1 November 2026 � 31 October 2031 Task Order Structure - Annual issuance of new, two-year non-severable Task Orders 4. Acquisition Authority & Strategy In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 5.1, this solicitation is an intended sole-source procurement. The Government will solicit and negotiate with only one source: Honeywell Aerospace (CAGE: 09128). This action is taken under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1. Market research�including Sources Sought Synopsis FA821425CBPIGA (posted 29 May 2025)�concluded that Honeywell Aerospace is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling the Government�s requirement without causing unacceptable delays to the MMIII weapon system mission. Note: While this is not a request for competitive proposals, information received from other responsible sources identifying their interest and capability will be considered solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future, at the Government�s discretion. 5. Proposal Submission Instructions All proposals submitted in response to this solicitation must be submitted electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. No other methods of proposal submission (e.g., email, hard copy, DoD SAFE) will be accepted. Offerors must be registered in PIEE and have the appropriate roles activated to submit proposals via the Solicitation module prior to the proposal due date. Cost & Pricing Data: The Government requests that ProPricer models (version v9.5.105.2) be submitted in conjunction with all Certified Cost and Pricing Data. Mandatory Pricing Rubric: Submission of the attached Pricing Rubric is a mandatory requirement. Proposals submitted without a completed Pricing Rubric will be automatically rejected by the PIEE solicitation module and will not be considered for evaluation. Submission Cutoff: Proposals will not be accepted after the solicitation closes. Timely submission is the sole responsibility of the offeror, and late proposals will not be evaluated unless otherwise stated under RFO guidelines.
