title: Metrology Grade Oscilloscope
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration (AFMETCAL) program office has a requirement to procure a highly accurate, standardized, metrology-grade oscilloscope to establish a consistent technical baseline across all Precision Measurement Equipment Laboratories (PMELs) and the AFMETCAL engineering laboratory. Historically, PMELs have independently procured various oscilloscopes categorized as Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE). This decentralized approach created significant inventory fragmentation, complicates Technical Order (TO) authoring/maintenance, and introduces training and bench setup inconsistencies across Air Force facilities. Standardizing hardware across all PMEL field units will ensure seamless technical alignment, simplify operator calibration training, streamline automated calibration routines, and guarantee identical bench setups across the enterprise. The Air Force is considering the purchase of 131 units to replace aging TMDE across active duty, guard, Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and PMEL locations. The Air Force is interested in any features that can shorten TACAN/IFF (pulse trains) measurements as well as integrated real-time measurement accuracy/uncertainty displayed during measurement. Although these are not part of the existing purchase description, they may be evaluated as part of a best value acquisition format. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 131 units over 4 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 26E-187A-RF in all correspondence. Responses are due by 12/3/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. Point of Contact � Megan Moretti Contract Specialist, Phone 937-713-5845 Email:megan.moretti@us.af.mil. Point of Contact - Frank Capuano, Contract Specialist, Phone 937-713-5842 Email:frank.capuano@us.af.mil.

title: DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) PHASE III GROUNDWATER TREATMENT PLANT CONSTRUCTION, NWIRP BETHPAGE, WANTAGH, NEW YORK
description: Solicitation Number: N4008527R0048 This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to make notice of a proposed contract action for performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Phase III Groundwater Treatment Plant Construction, Naval Weapons Industrial Reserve Plant (NWIRP) Bethpage, Wantagh, New York. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This Design-Bid-Build project aims to address a plume of contaminated groundwater that has spread south from the former NWIRP and Northrop Grumman properties. This contamination, primarily consisting of chlorinated VOCs (like TCE) and 1,4-dioxane, is being remediated as required by the Navy and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation. The core of this phase is the construction of a new Groundwater Treatment Plant (GWTP) designed to intercept the leading edge of the plume. The plant will treat the captured water to meet drinking water standards using a process that includes sand filters, an Advanced Oxidation Process (AOP), and Granular Activated Carbon (GAC). The scope of work involves the complete construction and commissioning of the facility. This includes completing three groundwater recovery wells and the associated underground piping to bring contaminated water to the plant. The facility itself will house numerous systems, including large storage tanks, multiple filter types, the AOP system, and granular activated carbon units. The project also covers the construction of two new buildings for the treatment plant and offices, along with all necessary structural, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure. The work includes: buried piping systems, pavements, and miscellaneous items; one underground vault; piping, valves, fittings for three recovery wells and wiring, instruments, and equipment within the conduit, manholes, and vaults; three Reinforced Plastic (FRP) vertical storage tanks; one glass fused Backwash waste steel tank; three Multimedia Vertical Pressure Filters (MMF) unit vessels, two Horizontal Cartridge Filters, one Ozone-Hydrogen Peroxide Advance Oxidation Process (AOP) system; three Liquid Phase Granular Activated Carbon (LGAC) unit vessels; eight pumps with piping, valves, supports and appurtenances; two blowers; chemical feed systems for Sodium Hydroxide, Sodium Hypochlorite and Hydrogen Peroxide; two buildings (treatment plant and office), foundations, and interior/exterior concrete slabs on grade and under-slab utility coordination; structural and architectural roof and systems; one 1200A, 277/480V, 3-phase, 3-Wire Service; an MCC for motor VFDs; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC); a PLC and SCADA system, and internet/cellular gateway to enable off- site Phase III System process parameters; earthwork, including pad excavation and site re-grading; site utilities; fencing; and a fire protection system. The completion time for this contract is 1,095 calendar days after award. This solicitation is being advertised as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. This source selection procurement requires both non-price (technical and past performance) and price proposals and will utilize the best value continuum process at FAR 15.103-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0048, Rev 1), Tradeoff approach. The basis for evaluation and evaluation factors for award will be included in the solicitation. Large business concerns are required to submit a subcontracting plan prior to award of the contract. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this project is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The anticipated award of this contract is March 2027. An SBA Small Business Search (SBS) and a Sources Sought Notice was conducted and issued on 21 January 2026, seeking eligible Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, and Women-Owned Small Businesses to determine the opportunity for a set-aside. The Government invited prospective offerors with the capabilities of performing construction services that meet or exceed the stated requirement to submit a capabilities statement. Respondents were required to submit relevant experience in performing efforts of similar size, scope, and complexity within the last seven (7) years. Based on the market research conducted for this procurement and in accordance with FAR 19.104-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0037, Rev 1), the Contracting Officer has determined that there is not a reasonable expectation that an adequate number of Small Business firms would respond to or be qualified to perform the requirements of this solicitation. Successful award and completion of the requirements can be achieved by soliciting the contract as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. A DD2579 Small Business Coordination Record was approved by the NAVFAC MIDLANT Small Business Professional on 30 March 2026. On 02 April 2026, the Small Business Administration (SBA) Procurement Center Representative (PCR) concurred with this recommendation. The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued by NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic CON22 on or about 03 December 2026. The solicitation number will be N4008527R0048. All documents will be in Adobe PDF file format and downloadable from the PIEE and Sam.gov website. The official address to the solicitation is https://piee.eb.mil and https://www.sam.gov. Contractors are encouraged to register for the solicitation when downloading from the website. Only registered contractors will be notified by email when amendments to the solicitation are issued. A free Acrobat Reader, required to view the PDF files, can be downloaded from the Adobe website. IMPORTANT NOTICE: All prospective offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). You must have an active registration in SAM to do business with the federal government. For additional information, go to https://www.sam.gov. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed by email to shayna.t.eichner.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Sonic Boom Launch Noise Analysis RFI _NAICS 541330, 541715
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposals (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. Facilities and infrastructure at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) are exposed to intense acoustic loads and sonic booms from an increasing cadence of launch operations. Existing historical data is primarily based on aircraft overflights and has limited applicability to the unique pressure signatures generated by modern launch vehicles (including Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Starship/Super Heavy, Vulcan, New Glenn, and other current or proposed vehicles). The Government requires development of a scientifically defensible material testing methodology and a predictive engineering model to evaluate the effects of launch noise and sonic booms on both current and legacy construction materials, infrastructure, and facility types at CCSFS. The effort shall support informed decisions on facility sustainment, retrofitting, or replacement. Reference the attached Statement of Objective for a more detailed description of this requirement. Please see attached RFI for further directions. Please respond to the questions found within the RFI document if interested no later than 3 December 2026, 2:00 PM EST. You may address questions in a narrative, annotated outline, bullet or table format. Thank you!

description: DESCRIPTION: This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice for project number 596A4-27-101 that requires Architect/Engineering (A/E) Design Services to Upgrade Fire Alarm System at the Lexington VA Healthcare System, Troy Bowling Campus. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. ONLY THE A/E FIRMS RESPONDING TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT BY SUBMITTING AN SF330 PACKAGE ON TIME WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR INITIAL EVALUATION. FOLLOWING INITIAL EVALUATION OF THE A/E FIRMS AND THEIR SF330S, A SOLICITATION FOR A PRICE PROPOSAL WILL BE SENT TO THE HIGHEST TECHNICALLY RATED A/E FIRM TO PROVIDE THE TYPE OF SERVICE(S) REQUIRED. The A/E Services contract that is anticipated to be awarded will be procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law 92- 582), Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 36.6 and VA Acquisition Regulation 836.6. In accordance with FAR 36.209 Construction Contracts With Architect-Engineer Firms , no contract for the construction of a project shall be awarded to the firm that designed the project or its subsidiaries or affiliates, except with the approval of the head of the agency or authorized representative. A/E DESIGN SERVICES SCOPE SYNOPSIS: The A/E will be required to perform comprehensive field investigations to base their design documents off of, this includes, above ceiling surveys that the VA will assist with access to all required spaces. Project will replace existing fire alarm system at the Troy Bowling Campus to include Building 1, Building 1A and Building 4. Replacement includes hospital space, parking garage as well as crawl space as required per code. Size of existing facility is 537,542 square feet. Existing fire alarm system is required to remain in service until new system is active and ready to be utilized. Phasing of cutover from existing to new system to be determined by A/E. Project will correct FCA Deficiencies 338139, 45058, 49003, 49909, 49035, 49963 and 49935. New fire alarm system will be required to interact with multiple systems throughout the hospital to include, but not limited to: Door magnets, elevators, HVAC systems, kitchen hood systems, sprinkler system, specialty fire suppression systems, door locking systems, smoke dampers, duct detectors and other systems. The estimated magnitude of construction for this A/E requirement is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. END OF DESIGN SCOPE SYNOPSIS Digital copies of the as-builts are limited. The consultant will be expected to fully investigate and confirm the validity of hard copy as-builts and other drawings. This will include independent investigation of the VAMC s flat files by the consultant to determine and procure the information required for the complete design. All offerors are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-73 the total cost of the architect or engineer services contracted for must not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of the construction project plus any fees for related services and activities. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-2 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action. Design limitation costs will be provided to the most highly rated AE firm selected to complete the design. Interested firms should submit their current SF-330 to matthew.whisman@va.gov. The SF-330s are due by December 3, 2026, at 2:00 PM (EST). Security Issues, Late Bids, Unreadable Offers Late submission of offers are outlined at FAR Parts 52.212-1(f), 52.214-7, and 52.215-1(c) (3).� Particular attention is warranted to the portion of the provision that relates to the timing of submission. Please see FAR 15.207(c) for a description of the steps the Government shall take with regard to unreadable offers. The virus scanning software used by our e-mail systems cannot always distinguish a macro from a virus. Therefore, sending a macro embedded in an e-mail message or an e-mail attachment may cause the e-mail offer to be quarantined. You may send both the spreadsheet and the spreadsheet saved in PDF format to ensure that your proposal is readable. Password protecting your offer is not permitted. The Contracting Officer will file the offer electronically which will allow access only by designated individuals. title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Mission Module Engineering and Technical Services
description: **ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION.*** Request for Proposal (RFP) (N6133127R0006) under the Seaport NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC), for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support. This effort has been previously been posted under the Opportunities page as the following: Sources Sought Notice (N6133126SNQ27), dated (Posted 7 May 2026) and the follow-up Advance Planning Notice/Pre-Solicitation Notice dated (16 June 2026). ***RESPONSES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE.*** ***ALL DOCUMENTS ARE AVAILABLE WITHIN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE*** Questions and Answers WILL TAKE PLACE THROUGH PIEE MODULE AND POSTED TO PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE BY ATTACHMENT***This is a solicitation for SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ONLY. This solicitation is to provide services to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) Modular Integration Division as the lead for engineering, analysis, and planning support for the modularization of off-board systems in support of the littoral warfare mission area. The requirements will include systems engineering, packaging and handling of off-board system hardware, system integration of legacy and emerging littoral mission systems, sea frame integration of mission modules, development of mission system common computing environments (e.g. Mission Package Computing Environment (MPCE)) and integrated communications networks (e.g. Multiple Vehicle Communication System(MVCS)), distributed engineering testing, and supporting the Government in validation and verification. Specifically, these requirements include the general program, engineering, technical, and integrated logistics support requirements for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS)Mission Modules (MM) program at NSWC PCD. Access to the solicitation is through the link. Access to the attachments are in the PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE through the link. The Solicitation number for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support is not N6133126R3111. The correct Solicitation number for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support is N6133127R0006.

title: Hydropower Technical Research & Knowledge Exchange
description: 1. General. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT for an upcoming Service Contract for HYDROPOWER TECHNICAL RESEARCH AND KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE. It is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER FAR SUBPART 5.2. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. Reponses to this Sources Sought announcement will be used by the Government to make business decisions and to inform potential future solicitations. a. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: 541990 - All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services b. The related size standard is: $19.5M c. Product Service Code is: R425 d. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � December 3, 2026 at 12:00pm Pacific Time. 2. Background. As the nation's leading hydropower asset owner and operator with 75 Corps owned hydropower projects across the U.S., USACE is charged with improving the capability, reliability, and safety of the Corps' hydropower infrastructure by developing or advancing state-of-the-art technology, innovative practices, and operational improvements. USACE's Hydroelectric Design Center (HDC) located in Portland, OR, Engineering Research and Development Center (ERDC) located in Vicksburg, MS, and the Hydropower R&D Advisory Committee (members from HDC, ERDC, HQ, and the Corps' 16 hydropower Districts) have taken the lead on managing the Hydropower R&D mission to include determining the industry needs, setting priorities, and managing the execution. 3. Project Scope. a. USACE Hydropower is conducting market research to identify available approaches for obtaining relevant technical information and research findings, exchanging technical knowledge with other owners and operators, and addressing shared technical problems. The government seeks access to technical research, practical guidance, and industry operating experience to support decisions concerning the design, operation, maintenance, protection, and modernization of hydropower facilities and associated electrical infrastructure. The anticipated areas of interest are: Hydropower equipment design, operation, maintenance, and associated best practices. Protection and control systems for hydropower facilities and associated electrical infrastructure. Economic evaluation and modeling of hydropower assets to support modernization planning. Potential approaches may include access to existing technical publications, technical exchanges, research services, collaborative investigations, training, or combinations of these services both virtually and through conference/workshop forums. b. Anticipated Period of Performance: January 01, 2027 � December 31, 2027 c. Number and Type of Contracts: NWP contemplates awarding one firm fixed price service contract. 4. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically (via email) with SUBJECT: Sources Sought � Hydropower Technical Research. Please email to Nicholas Weaver, Contract Specialist, at Nicholas.E.Weaver@usace.army.mil and Contracting Officer, at nicole.a.adams@usace.army.mil before 12:00PM Pacific Time on December 03, 2026. Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to six (6) pages and shall include the following information: Firm's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, CAGE and Unique Entity ID Firm's business category and size: Large Business (include summary of small business participation metrics), Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and at the subcontracting level, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). An explanation of the prime firm�s capabilities, special qualifications/certifications and equipment and describe the work to be self-performed as it pertains to the proposed work outlined in the Project Scope. In submitting capability statements for consideration, offers should address the following: i. Which capabilities you provide, how they are delivered, and any limitations on access or use. ii. Which of the three technical subject areas they support. iii. Describe available research, publications, technical exchanges, training, and research-participation opportunities. iv. Provide representative topics or examples sufficient to demonstrate relevance. v. Explain access arrangements, licensing restrictions, and internal-sharing limitations. vi. Distinguish services included in a standard offering from separately priced services. 4. Project Examples (for Joint Ventures, please include projects completed by the Joint Venture if available): i. To be considered for a potential set aside strategy, provide a maximum of three (3), minimum of one (1) project(s). These project examples must be similar in size, scope and complexity to the work described in paragraph 3 of this notice, with a description of each project (to include pertinent qualitative and quantitative information about featured scope elements), and include the following: Project Title Contract Number Contract award date Customer name, phone number and email address Prime or Subcontractor Initial contract dollar value Final contract dollar value Initial contract completion date Final contract completion date Customer satisfaction Note: The Government may verify information in CPARS or PPIRS. 5. Firm's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. 6. Firm's interest and the likelihood in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. (Refer to planned advertise and performance dates) 5. Disclaimer and Important Notes. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov to have size status considered. You must remain current for the duration of the source selection process to be eligible for award of a Government contract.

title: LOWER BRULE NORTH SHORELINE STABILIZATION AND ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, ELEMENT 2
description: The project is located along the left descending bank of Lake Sharpe near the Lower Brule, SD town site. Lower Brule North Element 2 includes a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, a riprap revetment to protect the shoreline and island from erosion, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island constructed in water up to three feet deep. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline will develop into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland, and this will also create approximately 32 acres of riparian habitat. Related tasks include earth moving, grading, bank shaping, rock installation, water management, fill, and topsoil placement.

THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. The purpose of this Market Research and Sources Sought Notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified Small Business, HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned, and Women Owned Small Business firms. Responses to this Sources Sought Synopsis will be used by the government in making appropriate acquisition decisions. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Mobile District, anticipates a future Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) procurement to acquire Architect-Engineer (AE) Services under individual task orders for Mobile Districts Environmental Quality (EQ) Program which meets the definition of AE Services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1101 and FAR 2.101 for Military, Civil, and Federal Agencies. The anticipated contracts will support military installations, Federal agencies, and other authorized customers, primarily within the Mobile Districts Area of Responsibility (AOR) and the South Atlantic Divisions (SAD) AOR. The Government anticipates a total program capacity of $600,000,000 over a five-year ordering period, allocated as follows: $500,000,000: Anticipated capacity for requirements administered by the USACE Mobile District. $100,000,000: Reserved capacity for use by other USACE districts within SAD to support mission-critical environmental requirements, including emerging or previously unplanned requirements not otherwise supported by existing contract vehicles. The anticipated capacity represents the maximum potential value of the procurement and does not constitute a guarantee of work or funding. The Government reserves the right to modify the acquisition strategy, contract structure, capacity allocation, and scope of the anticipated procurement based on market research findings and mission requirements. AE Services will provide a full range of comprehensive support for the Environmental Quality Program including but not limited to: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA); Clean Air Act (CAA); Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA); Clean Water Act (CWA); Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (CERCLA); National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); Energy Policy Act 2005; compliance; source reduction/waste minimization; conservation; restoration; Department of Defense Instruction; Executive Orders; policy, guidance, programmatic and operational program execution strategy; planning; permitting and technical support; environmental management systems; information technology tool refinement, customization, population and implementation; environmental training, outreach, strategy, and awareness; water compliance and reuse plans; vulnerability assessments; compliance assessments; multimedia and single media facility audits; environmental baseline surveys; DoD Services; Medical Departments and health services support; audits and assessments; planning studies and evaluations; geographic information system support; compliance monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting. Additional projects may include range and training program support, solid waste, RCRA evaluations, and management plans; DoD awards development; sustainability program initiatives and planning; ozone depleting substance (ODS) evaluations and elimination plans; energy studies and audits; facility evaluations and audits; Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) technical support and building commissioning; programmatic support of installation restoration and munitions response compliance cleanup programs; greenhouse gas initiatives; air quality monitoring, testing and permitting; air dispersion modeling; asbestos and lead-based paint sampling and report preparation; and real estate site assessments; perform Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Technical Assistance and Technical Review of planning and environmental products. Sources are being sought for firms with a North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code of 541330 with a Small Business Size Standard of no greater than $25,500,000 average annual receipts over five years. NO RESPONSES WILL BE ACCEPTED BY FAX OR MAIL. ALL RESPONSES MUST BE SENT via PIEE, DIRECTED to: Danielle Kachele and Kenneth Harlan. Should you have any questions, please reach out to Danielle Kachele at Danielle.l.kachele@usace.army.mil. Submittals are due no later than 2:00 pm CT on Thursday, December 3, 2026. Submittals will not be returned. Telephonic responses will not be honored. This is not a Request for Proposal, only a Request for Information. No award will result from this Sources Sought. This notice does not constitute any commitment by the Government. Note 1: This is not a Request for Proposal, only a Request for Information. No award will result from this Sources Sought. Note 2: This sources sought synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information solicited. Note 3: Large Businesses need not respond. *** End of Sources Sought Notice ***

title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: LOWER BRULE NORTH SHORELINE STABILIZATION AND ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, ELEMENT 2
description: The project is located along the right descending bank of Lake Sharpe near the Lower Brule, SD town site. Lower Brule North Element 2 includes a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, a riprap revetment to protect the shoreline and island from erosion, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island constructed in water up to three feet deep. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline will develop into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland, and this will also create approximately 32 acres of riparian habitat. Related tasks include earth moving, grading, bank shaping, rock installation, water management, fill, and topsoil placement.

description: Nákup a dodávka pevných paliv do kotelen v objektech doléčovacího střediska Horní Holčovice, 793 71, Holčovice, detašovaného pracoviště Psychiatrické nemocnice v Opavě, dle průběžných objednávek, s platností smlouvy (dobou plnění) nejpozději do 31. 12. 2027 nebo do vyčerpání finančního limitu smlouvy. title: Weapons Shipping Harness Refurbishment Blanket Purchase Agreement
description: This is a limited sources combined synopsis/solicitation for services prepared in accordance with simplified acquisition procedures found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13.2, effective 1 February 2026, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation/notice; further written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation Number N6278927Q0001 is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). The solicitation and incorporated provisions and clauses are in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 with an effective date of 13 March 2026. The Product and Service Code (PSC) is J019. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code is 336419. Supervisor of Shipbuilding Conversion and Repair, Groton CT (SSGR) intends to enter into a multiple award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), for a period of 5 years. The vendor shall refurbish weapon Shipping Harnesses in accordance with the attached specification. The Period of Performance shall be 27 January 2027 to 26 January 2032. Each BPA will have up to a five (5) year ordering period with a ceiling of up to $500,000. The BPA Call Limit will be $100,000. The ceiling of each agreement can be increased or decreased at any time by the Contracting Officer via bilateral modification to meet current and future requirements. Funding is not assigned to the BPA. The Government will only be obligated to the extent of calls placed against an awarded BPA. Each BPA call will be competed among the agreement holders as requirements arise. A call will then be placed based on the quote that is most advantageous to the Government. Offerors must provide a description of their property management system per FAR 45.201(c)(4) or confirmation of a property management system that has been reviewed and approved per DFARS 242.302 and meets the requirements of FAR 52.245-1(f). title: Supplemental F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Service Life Modification (SLM) Capacity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Program Office (PMA-265), is conducting market research to determine the industrial base�s existing capability and facility capacity to provide supplemental or secondary Service Life Modification (SLM) turnkey capacity for F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler aircraft starting in FY29. The Government seeks mature, currently operational�facilities, personnel, processes, tooling, and infrastructure capable of supporting SLM workload. The Government is not seeking conceptual or developmental solutions that would require significant new construction, extensive infrastructure development, or multi-year implementation before becoming operational. The Government currently executes these requirements through a hybrid framework utilizing the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) (The Boeing Company) and a Naval Aviation Enterprise organic depot (Fleet Readiness Center Southwest) under a public private partnership with the OEM. To support long-term strike fighter inventory requirements, the Government is evaluating the availability of additional commercial or second-source depot modification repair overhaul (MRO) capacity. Information submitted in response to this notice will assist the Government in determining its long-term acquisition strategy through 2038, including whether to establish an additional qualified source to supplement the current capacity or maintain the current hybrid framework mentioned above under the authority of FAR 6.103-3(b)(1) (Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy (DPCAP) Class Deviation (CD) 2026-O0017) / 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(3)(A) (Industrial Mobilization). PMA-265 anticipates a maximum SLM induction profile of up to 47 aircraft per year across the industrial base. Actual aircraft allocation among available sources may vary based on Fleet requirements, aircraft availability, demonstrated performance, schedule, and available capacity. 1. Scope of Interest The Government is seeking information on industry capability to perform the SLM workload to supplement current capacity, including but not limited to: Aircraft induction, preservation, inspection, and documentation; F/A-18E/F and EA-18G SLM Specification Modification work; Installation of applicable Structural Technical Directives (TDs) and Advanced Capability Modifications such as Block III upgrade kits; Procurement and management of all required material, including long-lead material, using corporate approaches that support anticipated year-of-execution requirements and ensure material is available for installation when required; Inspection-based repairs and structural modifications; Manufacturing or sourcing of repair parts and materials, as required; Aircraft systems troubleshooting and functional verification; Aircraft records and database updates; and Support for Functional Check Flights and coordination with Government representatives. The Government recognizes that individual respondents may be capable of supporting only a subset of this work or a limited annual quantity. Responses identifying supplemental capability, secondary capability, or potential teaming arrangements are encouraged. 2. Information Requested Interested firms are requested to provide the following information: I. Company Information Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Business size and applicable socioeconomic status, if any. Relevant experience performing MRO / depot-level maintenance, advanced avionic systems modification, modernization, structural repair, or sustainment work on tactical aircraft. II. Facility Information Location(s) of existing facilities proposed for this effort. Number, type, and dimensions of available aircraft bays or work positions, including usable floor area, hangar-door dimensions, overhead clearance, and any facility limitations. For planning purposes, the aircraft footprint is 45 feet wide by 61 feet long Availability of a suitable runway and airfield support for F/A-18 and EA-18G series aircraft. Current facility utilization and the earliest date capacity could be made available. Access to required security, quality assurance, tooling, material handling, and aircraft-support infrastructure. Current, or ability to obtain, Defense Security Services (DSS) facility clearance of Secret. Consistent with Executive Order 14372, Prioritizing the Warfighter in Defense Contracting, and the USW(A&S) memorandum, Prioritizing the Warfighter and Negotiation of Contractor Facilitation Costs (dated 4 May 2026), respondents shall identify whether they anticipate using their own capital to fund stand-up costs necessary to perform the proposed work and describe any Government support, reimbursement, or other enablers required to establish the proposed capability. III. Capacity and Throughput Maximum number of F/A-18E/F and/or EA-18G aircraft the company could induct and complete annually. Expected induction ramp-up profile by year. Estimated average turnaround time from induction through return to the Fleet. Constraints that may limit throughput, including workforce, facilities, supply chain, engineering support, tooling, or Government-furnished material. Ability to adjust capacity in response to changing Fleet requirements or surge demand. Availability of funds to purchase all material to protect quantity throughput and maintain a stock of consumables to perform repair incidents throughout the modification (such as addressing corrosion), parts managements to include obsolescence and manufacturing parts capability. IV. Technical Capability Experience with F/A-18-series aircraft or comparable military tactical aircraft. Capability to perform structural inspections, repairs, modifications, TD incorporation, Non-destructive Inspections (NDI), wiring/electrical work, and systems troubleshooting. Capability to manufacture repair parts or develop repair procedures when required, using Government- or original equipment manufacturer-provided engineering direction. Ability to manage material procurement, kit installation, consumables, and repair-incident-to-modification requirements. Experience coordinating with the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) or similar Government quality-assurance organizations. Ability to recruit, retain, and sustain sufficient qualified personnel to support anticipated SLM workload, including structural engineering personnel eligible for appointment as Naval Air Systems Command Designated Engineering Representatives (NAVDERs) to support the engineering analysis and disposition of aircraft-specific structural findings within the scope of authority delegated by NAVAIR. Respondents should describe their current and projected staffing capacity; recruitment, retention, and succession approaches; and ability to surge personnel as workload requires. V. Cybersecurity Ability to comply with applicable Department of the Navy, NAVAIR, and Department of War cybersecurity requirements for the protection, handling, storage, transmission, and access of Government information and data in performance of the proposed work. VI. Additional Information Identify any Government support, data, tooling, facilities, training, technical assistance, or other enablers that would be needed to establish or expand SLM capability. Provide any recommended acquisition, phasing, or transition approach that would help establish supplemental capacity while minimizing risk to Fleet readiness. 3. Response Instructions Responses should be limited to ten (10) pages and submitted electronically to jacob.r.heintze.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 3 December 2026. This RFI is issued for market research and planning purposes only. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to award a contract or reimburse any costs associated with responding. title: TRICARE Claims Review Services (TCRS)
description: INTRODUCTION: The Defense Health Agency (DHA), DHA Contracting Activity (DHACA), TRICARE Healthplans & Pharmacy Contracting Division (THPCD), is issuing this Request for Information pursuant to Class Deviation 2026-O0017, Revision 2 - Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 6 Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Attachment 2 - PGI 206.103-170 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The DHA intends to issue a sole-source bridge action to continue the provision of services provided under the existing TCRS contract, HT9402-17-D-0001, to Concept Plus. This contract modification to extend performance is necessary to continue to meet mission critical requirements and to support the transition to a competitively awarded follow-on TCRS contract. The base period of performance will be 6 months from March 01, 2027 � August 31, 2027 with an Option to Extend Services for an additional 6 months from September 1, 2027 � February 28, 2028. The extension is necessary to prevent a gap in support to critical DHA requirements after the end of the current TCRS contract on February 28, 2027, until a competitive follow-on contract is awarded, and the awardee completes transition-in. Background: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) supports health services for more than 9.4 million beneficiaries of the Military Health System (MHS). The purpose of the TCRS contract is to assist the DHA Improper Payment Evaluation Branch (IPEB) in identifying and reporting improper payments and discrepancies in payment recording for the MHS. TCRS support provides an independent impartial review of claims processing procedures and reimbursement methodologies utilized by purchased-care contractors and assesses purchased-care contractor compliance with TRICARE policies and directives by evaluating the accuracy of claims payment and payment record coding for the MCSC, TMEP, TPharm, TOP, and ADDP contracts. TCRS helps support IPEB�s requirement to assess the potential risk of improper payments and to identify and report improper payments to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for publication in the Department of Defense (DoD) Agency Financial Report (AFR) pursuant to Public Laws 107-300, and the Payment Integrity Act of 2019 (PIIA), Public Laws 116-117. A new contractor would require a minimum of 6 months to complete the transition-in requirements given the startup requirements associated with staff recruiting and training, meeting the Personnel Security, and System Security and connectivity requirements. The current TCRS contractor, Concept Plus, is the only known contractor that can provide these services within the needed time frame. AUTHORITY: DHACA TRICARE Healthplans & Pharmacy Contracting Division (THPCD) is issuing this Request for Information for the purpose of market research prior to releasing a sole-source bridge action as required by CD 2026-O0017, Rev 2, Attachement 2 - PGI 206.103-170. DISCLAIMER AND IMPORTANT NOTES: THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Any proposals submitted will not receive a response. This notice solely constitutes a market research effort, for informational purposes only, as described under RFO 10.001. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a potential contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right to use results of the communications with industry for any purpose consistent with and not otherwise prohibited by RFO Part 10. NEXT STEPS: Interested parties wishing to submit a relevant capabilities statement with information demonstrating experience with reviewing/auditing healthcare claims must make their submittals, no more than 5 pages, to the Government via email to the Primary Point of Contact (below) not later than 2pm Mountain Standard Time (MST) on December 03, 2026. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization�s qualifications to perform healthcare claims reviews. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: Please respond or submit inquiries (via email) to the Defense Health Agency, TRICARE Healthplans & Pharmacy Contracting Division, TRICARE Support Branch, support contractor Mr. Justin O�Hara at justin.a.ohara2.ctr@health.mil. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. CONFIDENTIALITY: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. Industry responses will be shared with DHA staff for the purpose of market research. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s). title: H146--Dental Waterline Testing
description: This Solicitation shall result in a firm fixed-price contract for a period of one (1) base year and three (3) option years upon award. The contractor shall provide quarterly Heterotrophic Plate Count (HPC) 2-day testing services for Dental Unit Water Lines (DUWLs) at the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, located at 1481 W. 10th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46202. The purpose of this testing is to determine the Colony Forming Units (CFUs) present in the water supplied through the Dental Clinic's waterline system and ensure compliance with applicable water standards. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, and supervision necessary to perform the required dental waterline testing services. The contractor shall coordinate testing requirements with the COR at the beginning of each quarter to determine the number of tests required. Contractor personnel shall collect water samples from functional dental unit water lines after clinic hours to minimize disruption to patient care and shall provide a minimum of twenty-four (24) hours advance notice to VA Dental personnel prior to sample collection. Test results shall be provided electronically to the COR or designated VA Dental personnel within five (5) business days of receipt of the samples. Any retesting required due to contractor-caused delays resulting in sample expiration shall be performed at no additional cost to the Government. All testing shall be performed in accordance with the Infection Control Standards for VA Dental Clinics Guidelines. HPC waterline testing should be conducted by a laboratory certified by the EPA or applicable state authority to perform environmental testing. The contractor shall ensure all personnel are qualified and experienced in performing water quality testing services. Services shall be performed Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays, and in coordination with VA Dental Clinic operations. This procurement has been set aside 100 percent for Small Business concerns. Offers from firms other than Small Business concerns will not be considered and shall be rejected. NAICS Code 541380, Testing Laboratories and Services, applies. The applicable size standard is $19 Million. The anticipated award date is December 18, 2026, for a one (1) year base period with three (3) one (1) year option periods. Solicitation packages will be available on or about November 18, 2026. Electronic solicitations may be obtained at no cost from SAM.gov. All questions shall be submitted in writing to Jacob J. Bishop, Contract Specialist, at jacob.bishop@va.gov. Questions will be answered through solicitation amendment only. No telephone requests will be accepted. Quotations shall be submitted by email to jacob.bishop@va.gov no later than the date and time specified in the solicitation. The anticipated period of performance is December 22, 2026, through December 21, 2030, inclusive of all option periods

title: TRICARE Claims Review Services (TCRS)
description: DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY (DHA) Notice of Intent Description: Government�s Notice of Intent (NOI) to extend the TRICARE Claims Review Services (TCRS) contract performed by Concept Plus for up to 12 months. The work includes evaluating the accuracy of claims payment and payment record coding under the terms of the TRICARE Claims Review Services contract. A solicitation document will not be issued, nor will quotations be requested. The Defense Health Agency (DHA), DHA Contracting Activity (DHACA), TRICARE Healthplans & Pharmacy Contracting Division (THPCD), is issuing this NOI pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.2. The DHA intends to issue a sole-source bridge action to continue the provision of services provided under the existing TCRS contract, HT9402-17-D-0001, to Concept Plus in accordance with Class Deviation 2026-O0017, Revision 2 - Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 6 Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Attachment 2 - PGI 206.103-170 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This contract modification to extend performance is necessary to continue to meet mission critical requirements and to support the transition to a competitively awarded follow-on TCRS contract. A new contractor would require a minimum of 6 months to complete the transition-in requirements given the startup requirements associated with staff recruiting and training, meeting the Personnel Security, and System Security and connectivity requirements. The current TCRS contractor, Concept Plus, is the only known contractor that can provide these services within the needed time frame. The base period of performance will be from March 01, 2027 � August 31, 2027, with a 6 month Option to Extend Services from September 1, 2027 � February 28, 2028, for a total bridge extension of 12 months. The extension is necessary to prevent a gap in support to critical DHA requirements after the end of the current TCRS contract on February 28, 2027, until a competitive follow-on contract is awarded, and the awardee completes transition-in. Interested Parties: Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar services described in this notice may submit a capability statement, no more than 5 pages, outlining their capability to perform the described work. Capability Statements must be received within the time set forth in this synopsis to be considered by the Government. The determination to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Defense Health Agency (DHA) supports health services for more than 9.4 million beneficiaries of the Military Health System (MHS). The purpose of the TCRS contract is to assist the DHA Improper Payment Evaluation Branch (IPEB) in identifying and reporting improper payments and discrepancies in payment recording for the MHS. TCRS support provides an independent impartial review of claims processing procedures and reimbursement methodologies utilized by purchased-care contractors and assesses purchased-care contractor compliance with TRICARE policies and directives by evaluating the accuracy of claims payment and payment record coding for the MCSC, TMEP, TPharm, TOP, and ADDP contracts. TCRS helps support IPEB�s requirement to assess the potential risk of improper payments and to identify and report improper payments to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for publication in the Department of Defense (DoD) Agency Financial Report (AFR) pursuant to Public Laws 107-300, and the Payment Integrity Act of 2019 (PIIA), Public Laws 116-117. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: Please respond or submit inquiries (via email) to Gregory Stephens at gregory.r.stephens3.civ@health.mil. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 10,000 CUYD 25101-0300 Placed Riprap, Class 3: 1,725 CUYD 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 5,140 TON 40101-5600 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Gyratory Mix, 1/2-Inch or 3/4-Inch Nominal Maximum Size Aggregate, 0.3 To <3 Million ESAL: 8,300 TON 55201-0200 Structural Concrete, Class A (AE): 752 CUYD 55401-2000 Reinforcing Steel, Epoxy Coated: 138,000 LB 55601-1100 Bridge Railing, Steel, Two Rail: 642 LNFT 56501-0200 Drilled Shaft, 24-Inch Diameter: 750 LNFT 56501-0300 Drilled Shaft, 30-Inch Diameter: 890 LNFT 60901-1300 Curb, Concrete, 15-Inch Depth (Reinforced, Colored): 3,921 LNFT 61701-4500 Guardrail System Mgs, Type 2, Class A Steel Posts: 1,290 LNFT 63506-0500 Temporary Traffic Control, Flagger: 5,800 HOUR ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � November 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � December 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 This will be solicited as a full and open competition.

description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source HT941027N0014 THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE ORDER CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division � San Diego (HCD-SD), Echo Branch intends to award a firm fixed price five (5)-Year Purchase order RFO 12.102 (b) for acquisitions valued over the SAT, only one source being available to meet the Government�s needs, to: ORTHO CLINICAL DIAGNOSTICS SINGAPORE PTE LTD, KOREA BRANCH 366 HANGANG-DAERO YONGSAN-GU, SEOUL, 04323 SOUTH KOREA UEI: JNSJRDQQH2J6 CAGE: 767DF The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 325413 - Pharmaceutical Preparation Manufacturing; the business size standard is 1,250 (in number of employees). The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6550 � Invitro Diagnostics Substances Reagents The objective of this sole source award is to procure Chemistry/Immunology Reagents with Analyzer for Brian D. Allgood Army Community Hospital, South Korea for the Department of Pathology. The contractor-furnished chemistry and immunology analyzers shall be capable of providing complete chemistry and immunochemistry testing. The entire analyzer system shall be serviced and supplied through a single Contractor awarded the contract, including all parts, equipment, and supplies not manufactured, provided, or serviced directly by the Contractor. The system shall provide redundancy to ensure continuous operations. Each analyzer shall have the capacity to perform both chemistry and immunology assays. The Contractor shall provide the system, training, supplies, reagents, unscheduled maintenance, and preventive maintenance. All equipment displays and supporting literature shall be in English. The Contractor shall include delivery, installation, all calibrators and standards, reagents and reagent packs, and quality-control materials necessary to perform the specified assays. The Contractor shall also perform initial method validations in accordance with Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. The Contractor shall remove the analyzers upon contract termination. Rationale Justifying: Ortho Clinical Diagnostics Singapore Pte. Ltd., Korea Branch, a division of QuidelOrtho Corporation, is the sole manufacturer capable of providing clinical chemistry and integrated chemistry/immunoassay analyzers that meet the Government�s test-volume requirements without requiring a facility water supply. The Defense Health Agency requires analyzers that use 100 percent waterless, dry-slide technology. These sites cannot receive reagent-grade water into the facility for safe, quality laboratory testing and are not approved by the state to discharge biohazardous waste into any drain. This technology is unique to QuidelOrtho�s VITROS� line of analyzers and is essential to meeting the agency�s operational and mission requirements for the following reasons: Infrastructure Independence: VITROS dry-slide technology eliminates the need for water, plumbing, and drains. This is a critical advantage in military healthcare environments, where logistical footprints must be minimized. It ensures operational continuity and significantly reduces infrastructure dependencies. Enhanced Quality and Reliability: The system uses disposable tips for each sample, eliminating the risk of sample-to-sample carryover and reagent-to-reagent contamination that can occur in traditional wet-chemistry systems. This supports the accuracy and reliability of test results for patient care, particularly for high-acuity, time-sensitive assays. For example, emergency physicians rely on rapid, accurate first-run results for high-sensitivity troponin to triage potential heart attacks; procalcitonin and lactic acid to diagnose life-threatening sepsis; and potassium levels to treat sudden acute renal or metabolic failure. In these life-threatening situations, a false or contaminated initial result can delay critical medical intervention. The dry-slide technology�s elimination of sample carryover helps ensure that providers can rely on the initial result when time is of the essence. Laboratory Productivity: Reagents are self-contained in a dry-slide format that provides calibration stability of up to six months for most assays. This extended calibration interval substantially reduces the time and labor associated with daily calibration and quality-control procedures while also reducing reagent waste.systems. This ensures the highest accuracy and reliability of test results for patient care, which is absolutely critical for high-acuity, time-sensitive assays. For example, emergency physicians rely on rapid, flawless first-time results for high sensitivity troponin to triage imminent heart attacks, procalcitonin and lactic acid to diagnose life-threatening sepsis, and potassium levels to treat sudden acute renal or metabolic failure. In these life-or-death scenarios, a false or contaminated first read delays vital medical interventions; the dry-slide technology's elimination of sample carryover ensures providers can trust the initial result when time is of the essence. Laboratory Productivity: Reagents are self-contained in a dry-slide format that provides up to a six-month calibration stability for most assays. This extended frequency drastically reduces the time and labor spent on daily calibration and quality control procedures while decreasing reagent waste. This effort includes, but is not limited to, integration, engineering and logistics support of engineering investigations, training, publication development, support equipment procurements (that are the results of Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) efforts) and support equipment repair, development and validation of change kits, change kit procurement and change kit installation, engineering services, sustaining or production engineering support, logistic modeling and analysis, technical representative field services, and non-recurring engineering for design, development, prototyping, validation, and testing. The products developed are Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) (Class I/II), manufacturing and maintenance process changes, inspection techniques, changes in operational procedures and publications changes. title: Design-Build Modernization of the LPOE in Lynden, Washington Sources Sought
description: KENNETH G. WARD (LYNDEN) LAND PORT OF ENTRY The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service Capital Construction Branch is seeking capable and experienced Design-Build firms for the modernization of the Land Port of Entry, located in Lynden, Washington through this Sources Sought notice. The Land Port of Entry in Lynden Washington, occupying approximately 10.3 acres, is located along the US-Canadian border at the northern end of Washington State Route (SR) 539 (aka Guide-Meridian Road). The port, which is approximately six miles north of the city of Lynden, Washington, is located approximately ten miles to the east of the Peace Arch and Pacific Highway Land Ports of Entry (which are in nearby Blaine Washington), and is located approximately ten miles to the west of the Sumas Land Port of Entry. The existing port in Lynden was last modernized in the late 1980s. This announcement is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposals, or offer. No contract will be awarded from this notice. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of information in response to this notice.

title: Hankintailmoitus: LapIT Oy:n vakuutusturvan hankinnan kilpailutus
description: Hankintailmoitus: LapIT Oy:n vakuutusturvan hankinnan kilpailutus LapIT Oy (myöhemmin Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia vakuutusturvasta ja siihen liittyvistä palveluista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. LapIT Oy:n vakuutusturva ja sen laajuus on kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Ensimmäinen vakuutuskausi on 1.1.2027-31.12.2027. Tämän jälkeen vakuutuskausi on kalenterivuosi. Tarjous jätetään alkaen täydestä kalenterivuodesta (2027). LapIT Oy:llä on oikeus vakuutuskausien aikana kilpailuttaa vakuutukset uudelleen ja siirtää vakuutukset kilpailutuksen voittajalle. Vakuutukset ovat voimassa toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. title: Työterveyspalveluiden hankinta
description: Työterveyspalveluiden hankinta HANKINNAN KOHDE Hankinnan kohteena ovat SUEKin henkilöstön työterveyspalvelut. Tavoitteena on oikea-aikainen hoito, työn terveysriskien ehkäisy, työkyvyn ylläpito, hoidon jatkuvuus ja ennakoitavat kokonaiskustannukset. Palvelut määritellään toiminnallisina vaatimuksina, eivätkä ne edellytä tietyn toimittajan tuotetta tai järjestelmää. Hankinnan kohteena olevat työterveyshuollon palvelut kuuluvat julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetun lain (1397/2016, jäljempänä hankintalaki) liitteen E kohdassa 1 tarkoitettuihin sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluihin. Näihin palveluihin sovelletaan hankintalain 25 §:n 1 momentin 3 kohdassa säädettyä 400 000 euron kansallista kynnysarvoa. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvonlisäveroton kokonaisarvo koko sopimuskaudelta, mahdolliset optiokaudet mukaan lukien, alittaa edellä mainitun kynnysarvon. Hankinta kilpailutetaan siten pienhankintana, eikä siihen sovelleta hankintalain mukaisia kilpailuttamismenettelyjä. Hankinnassa noudatetaan tässä hankintailmoituksessa ja tarjouspyynnössä kuvattua menettelyä sekä hankintayksikön hankintaohjeita ja muuta sovellettavaa lainsäädäntöä. Tilaajan toimipaikka sijaitsee osoitteessa Valimotie 10, 00380 Helsinki. Tilaajan palveluksessa on tarjouspyynnön laatimishetkellä 18 henkilöä. Henkilöstömäärä voi muuttua sopimuskauden aikana. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tiettyyn henkilöstö- tai palvelujen käyttömäärään. Palvelut koskevat kulloinkin tilaajan ilmoittamia työterveyshuollon piiriin kuuluvia työntekijöitä. Palveluntuottajalla tulee olla käytettävissään vähintään kolme (3) työterveyshuollon lähivastaanottopistettä pääkaupunkiseudulla, joista yhden tulee olla palvelujen käytännön saavutettavuuden kannalta tarkoituksenmukaisesti saavutettavissa tilaajan toimipaikasta Valimotie 10, Helsinki. Lisäksi tilaajan palveluksessa työskentelee henkilöitä myös Tampereella, joten palveluntuottajalla tulee olla lisäksi käytettävissään vähintään yksi (1) työterveyshuollon lähivastaanottopiste Tampereella. Hankinta muodostaa yhden kokonaisuuden, joten SUEK valitsee vain yhden sopijakumppanin. Kokonaisuutena hankkimista perustellaan ehkäisevän työterveyshuollon, sairaanhoidon, työkyvyn tuen ja potilastietojen jatkuvuuden yhteensovittamisella. Ryhmittymänä tarjoaminen ja alihankinta sallitaan. Osatarjouksia ja vaihtoehtoisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä,

title: Geostationary extReme UltraViolet Imager (GRUVI), Instrument Request for Information
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This RFI seeks information from industry regarding capabilities, interest, and options for providing a solar observing Space Weather (SW) Next Geostationary extReme UltraViolet Imager (GRUVI) Instrument for a future operational NOAA Space weather mission that can resolve solar features, including coronal holes, filaments and prominences, active regions, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and X10 Class solar flares which will be used by the National Weather Service and the NOAA Space Weather Predication Center to generate and provide Space Weather forecasts and alerts. Solar GRUVI imagery will provide comprehensive situational awareness of the inner solar corona. Although there is no requirement for the number of GRUVI spectral bands, bands will be selected that are sensitive to different plasma temperatures within the range specified for feature and phenomenological discrimination. It is anticipated that at the conclusion of this Phase A study any industry partner will be prepared to enter directly into a System Requirements Review (SRR), approximately one month after Implementation contract award, followed by a Preliminary Design Review (PDR). The capabilities required to perform this Phase A Study for the GRUVI instrument are not currently within the NASA/NOAA workforce, thus the government requires contractor support to perform this study. It is the plan that in the future the capabilities being sought by the RFI will be identified in house, which would allow the government to leverage using our own work force. In addition this RFI will allow the Government to assess contractor capability to manufacture the GRUVI instrument. The Government anticipates multiple awards for the Formulation/Risk reduction phase of the contract. Further, since this is planned to be a fixed price contract the government may authorize the use of priced, or unpriced option to add additional scope or extend the period of performance should the RFI result in the formation of the contract for the GRUVI instrument. The only unique attribute is that the Government will consider a pre-priced option proposed by a contractor to retire additional implementation risk. All responses, comments and/or questions shall be submitted electronically via email to Kelly Lytton at kelly.r.lytton@nasa.gov no later than 5:00pm EDT December 3, 2026.

description: Project Title: Tactical Communication Systems Procurement, Services & Sustainment (TCS-PSS) Reference Number: CSO-ARMY-TCS-PSS-2027 Primary NAICS: 334220 � Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing 1. This initiative seeks to secure a mix of single-award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts and/or Other Transactions (OTs) to streamline the procurement, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of both legacy systems and emerging transport hardware and software. Focused on supporting Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2), the effort aims to deliver highly secure�National Security Agency (NSA) High Assurance certified or Sensitive but Unclassified - Encrypted (SBU-E) qualified�resilient, and interoperable communication systems. To counter future cryptographic threats, the framework is seeking capable vendors to provide a plan for incorporating Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) compliant algorithms and achieving National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) validation by 31 December 2030, ensuring robust data protection and mission command resilience in contested joint and coalition environments. 2. description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This RFI seeks information from industry regarding capabilities, interest, and options for providing a solar observing Space Weather (SW) Next Geostationary extReme UltraViolet Imager (GRUVI) Instrument for a future operational NOAA Space weather mission that can resolve solar features, including coronal holes, filaments and prominences, active regions, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and X10 Class solar flares which will be used by the National Weather Service and the NOAA Space Weather Predication Center to generate and provide Space Weather forecasts and alerts. The capabilities required to perform this Phase A Study for the GRUVI instrument are not currently within the NASA/NOAA workforce, thus the government requires contractor support to perform this study. title: VectorNav VN100T-CR Sensors - Brand Name, Single Source
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Eastern Acquisition Division, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a single-source basis to VectorNav Technologies, LLC, for twenty-two (22) VectorNav VN100T-CR sensors in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b)(1), which permits soliciting from a single source when only one source is reasonably available to satisfy the Government�s requirements. Sole Source Justification: The National Data Buoy Center (NDBC) requires twenty-two (22) VectorNav VN100T-CR sensors to support its operational weather buoy systems. These sensors provide measurements of Earth�s magnetic field, acceleration, and angular rotation, which are processed into directional wave products used by the National Weather Service (NWS) and the Global Telecommunication System (GTS). The sensors are intended to replace the obsolete Lord MicroStrain 3DM-GX1 sensors currently utilized in NDBC�s operational systems. NDBC modified its wave system interface firmware to accommodate the VN100T-CR sensor�s input data stream and conducted laboratory and field testing to confirm compatibility and proper operation. The VN100T-CR has since been integrated into NDBC�s operational buoy systems. Acquiring an alternative brand would require additional modifications to existing mounting configurations and interface firmware, as well as repeating laboratory and field testing. These changes would result in additional costs to the Government and could interrupt NDBC�s ability to maintain continuous wave observations. Accordingly, the VectorNav VN100T-CR is required to maintain compatibility with existing equipment, avoid unnecessary duplication of costs, and support continuity of NDBC�s operational mission. Notice to Interested Parties: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation package is available. However, interested parties that believe they can satisfy the Government�s requirements may submit a written capability statement and supporting documentation demonstrating their ability to provide the specified VectorNav VN100T-CR sensors. Responses must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist identified in this notice no later than 12/03/2026. All submissions will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct the acquisition on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition, based upon responses received, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice.

description: a) Vývoj řídicího panelu cloudové aplikace Solene-cloud v podobě grafické webové nebo desktopové aplikace, která bude obsahovat ovládací prvky pro veškeré funkce, které bude Solene-cloud svým uživatelům nabízet. Řídicí panel bude sloužit zejména k zadávání vstupních parametrů simulací spouštěných v cloudu AWS, k volbě výpočetního výkonu (tj. času potřebného pro simulaci) a k volbě charakteru výstupních výsledků.
